aboutPreview.title: I did not begin in psychology.
paragraphs:
I'm a psychotherapist, counsellor and coach. I work with people who are carrying something, anxiety, grief, burnout, a marriage that's gone quiet, a version of themselves they don't recognise anymore.

Most of them are managing. That's usually the problem. They're functioning well enough that nobody's asked how they are in a long time.

How I got here

I didn't start in psychology. Most of my working life has been in security and risk — and I'm still in it. It's not a past career I left behind for something more meaningful. I do both.

People find that combination odd until they think about it. Security work puts you around people on their worst days: after the incident, during the emergency, in the hours when things have gone wrong and someone has to stay calm. I spent years doing that before I ever sat in a therapy room.

What I kept noticing was how many people were handling enormous things without any support at all. Not because help didn't exist, but because asking felt like admitting something. So I went and trained properly  [PhD, Psychology, INSTITUTION, YEAR], then [COACHING CERTIFICATION, BODY, YEAR] — and built a practice alongside the work I was already doing.

I've been doing both ever since. The security work keeps me around real pressure. The practice is where I do something about it.
aboutPreview.quote: “Catastrophes are almost never sudden. They are the visible moment of a failure that has been quietly accumulating somewhere nobody was looking.”

services.title: Six ways to work together
services.intro: Every one of them starts the same way — a free fifteen-minute conversation, with no charge, no obligation, and nothing on record.

assessments.title: Two instruments, both free
assessments.intro: Neither is a diagnosis and neither will tell you what to do. They show you, in writing, where you are solid and where you are thin — which is the only place real work can start.

cards.title: The Self-Audit
cards.body: Before you assess anyone else, assess yourself. Five dimensions — self-knowledge, regulation, inherited patterns, capacity, and repair.

cards.title: The Relational Risk Assessment
cards.body: Where is your relationship exposed, and what happens when that point fails? The five exposure points that account for most of what arrives in my room.

beliefs.title: Four things I will say out loud

process.title: Four steps, and you can stop at any of them
process.intro: Nothing here is a commitment you cannot withdraw from. The first step costs nothing and goes nowhere on record.

letter.title: One letter a month. No noise.
letter.intro: One idea from the practice, written properly, sent once a month. No sequences, no upsells, and you can leave in one click.

closing.intro: Fifteen minutes, no charge, no obligation. You describe what is happening; I tell you honestly whether I am the right person for it — and if I am not, who is.
